entities.summary: Sanzō Nosaka  was a Japanese writer, editor, labor organizer, communist agent, politician, and university professor and a founder of the Japanese Communist Party (JCP). He was the son of a wealthy Japanese merchant, and attended Keio University. While in university, Nosaka became interested in social movements, and joined a moderate labor organization after graduation, working as a research staff member, and as a writer and editor of the organization's magazine. He traveled to Britain in 1919 to study political economy, where he deepened his studies of Marxism and became a confirmed communist.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a founder of the Japanese Communist Party and a prominent labor organizer, Sanzō Nosaka played a key role in shaping Japan's communist movement and influencing its labor policies. His work had significant regional impact, contributing to the country's transition from an imperialist society to a more socialist-oriented nation.
